_law: A phase closes only when its exit_test is RUN and its result recorded here. 'Done' with no recorded run is not done.
Every close triggers a REVIEW that must return a verdict per remaining phase: keep / change / drop — with a reason. A review that changes nothing must SAY it changed nothing and why.
The plan may be wrong. Dropping a phase with a recorded reason is a correct outcome, not a failure.
No phase may be marked done because its work was performed. It is done when the test that could have failed did not.

work._progress_2026-08-10:
PART DONE BY A DIFFERENT ROUTE THAN THIS ITEM PROPOSED, and the item stays open for the half that is left.

WHAT MEASURING FIRST FOUND. `_proc_wood` already generates plank bands. Its `Wave.Scale` was 1.6 against OBJECT coordinates, which are local metres here — a **625 mm plank pitch**. A 2 m wardrobe carcass showed three bands and a drawer front showed part of one, so 163 objects got a flat wash of a texture that was 3.5x too large to read as grain. The grain was never missing. Pitch is now physical and named: PLANK_PITCH_MM 180, GRAIN_FEATURE_MM 40. The A/B is unambiguous by eye.

WHY THE PHOTOGRAPHIC HALF IS STILL OPEN, with the number that decides it: signed oak #C7B896 is linear (0.571, 0.479, 0.305); the mean of wood_floor_Diffuse_2k is linear (0.217, 0.117, 0.055). The tint route `_pbr_material` uses would need a multiply of (2.64, 4.10, 5.57) to reach the signed colour — brightening a dark map up to 5.6x, which crushes the light end of the grain to white. **The photographic route needs a texture whose mean is already near the target, and neither shelf has a light oak.** That is a fetch (Poly Haven has ~90 texture sets beyond our 9) or a different operator (modulate the signed colour by the map's luminance, the way `_woven` already does for fabric) — not a tint.

AND A KNOB WAS BUILT AND DELETED IN THE SAME SITTING. A metric said our band contrast was 4.07x a photograph of real oak; a `grain_amp` of 0.25 moved it to 3.98x, which looked like the metric was stable. The crop was not: the 0.25 pass was visibly back to flat beige. The metric's high-pass window was wider than the bands it measured, so it subtracted its own signal. I believed the metric over the eye. The knob is gone and the story is in the code where the next person will read it.
